security_audit.summary: All 60 static findings are false positives in context. The commands, network calls, environment reads, filesystem tests, documentation backticks, and heuristic bracket patterns support the documented Jira and Bitbucket workflow; no prompt injection or data exfiltration evidence was found.

remediation.issue: The skill performs Jira and Bitbucket writes when --apply is supplied.
remediation.suggestion: Keep preview mode as the default, require explicit user authorization for --apply, and continue verifying every created or changed resource.

remediation.issue: API credentials are read from environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Use a credential manager or short-lived tokens with the minimum Jira and Bitbucket permissions required.

remediation.issue: A local repository is used for branch operations.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the repository path and origin validation, and reject symlinked or unexpected clones before any push.

remediation.issue: The static analyzer flags test literals and documentation examples as suspicious patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Exclude tests and documentation from malware heuristics or retain context-aware rules so future audits remain actionable.

content.user_title: Create verified Jira issues and branches
content.value_statement: Creating a Jira issue and matching repository branches can leave assignment, status, or sprint incomplete. This skill previews the plan, performs only requested writes, and verifies the resulting issue and branches.
actual_capabilities: Preview a new Jira issue before any write.
Create a Jira issue with a validated summary, description, project, type, assignee, and status.
Resolve the single active sprint and verify assignment, status, and sprint membership.
Plan Bitbucket branches from repository branching models and existing issue-key branches.
Fetch the selected base commit and push a new branch without switching the local worktree.
Read back the issue and remote branches before reporting success.
limitations: Requires Python 3.10 or newer, the requests package, and private workflow configuration.
Supports Jira Cloud and Bitbucket Cloud through configured credentials and workspace settings.
Creates or updates only explicitly requested issues and branches; it does not commit, merge, deploy, or post Slack messages.
Cannot resolve missing requirements, multiple active sprints, or multiple matching branches without user input.

use_cases.title: Report a verified defect
use_cases.description: Create a Bug issue with observed and expected behavior, assign it, and place it in the active sprint.

use_cases.title: Start approved development work
use_cases.description: Create or reuse an issue and add matching branches in the requested repositories.

use_cases.title: Review before writing
use_cases.description: Generate a read-only issue and branch plan before authorizing the requested changes.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a new issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview a Jira Task named Show saved inventory items. Include the observed problem and expected result. Do not create it.

prompt_templates.title: Create one issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the approved Jira Bug from request.json. Assign it to the authenticated user, use To Do, and verify the active sprint.

prompt_templates.title: Add repository branches
prompt_templates.prompt: Use existing issue DEMO-1 and preview bugfix branches in the service and web repositories. Reuse any branch that already contains the issue key.

prompt_templates.title: Create and verify both
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the approved issue, then create feature branches from the development base in the requested repositories. Verify assignee, status, sprint, and each remote branch before reporting URLs.

output_examples.input: Preview a Task for missing saved inventory items.
output_examples.output: The preview lists a Task, the authenticated assignee, To Do status, and one active sprint. It reports the requested repository without creating the issue or branch.

output_examples.input: Create branches for DEMO-1 in service.
output: The issue is a Bug assigned to the authenticated user and already in the active sprint.
The planned branch is bugfix/DEMO-1-missing-items from the development base.
After approval, the helper verifies the remote branch and returns its Bitbucket URL.

best_practices: Run the preview first and add apply only after the issue content and repository scope are approved.
Store configuration and API tokens outside the repository and grant only the required permissions.
After a timeout or partial failure, search for the existing issue and resume with its key.
anti_patterns: Do not rerun issue creation blindly after an unknown response.
Do not add repositories that were not included in the requested scope.
Do not force-push, delete and recreate a branch, or switch the user worktree.

faq.question: Does reading an issue create anything?
faq.answer: No. Passing only an issue key stays read-only, even when apply is present.

faq.question: When are writes performed?
faq.answer: Writes occur only for explicitly requested operations after the apply option is added.

faq.question: Which services are supported?
faq.answer: The helpers support configured Jira Cloud and Bitbucket Cloud workspaces.

faq.question: How are credentials supplied?
faq.answer: Jira and Bitbucket credentials come from environment variables, not request files or source code.

faq.question: What happens with multiple sprints or branches?
faq.answer: The helper stops and asks for the intended target instead of guessing.

faq.question: Does it commit or merge code?
faq.answer: No. It only creates or reuses the requested issue and remote branch references.
